label: ALCE evaluates fluency, correctness and citation quality
summary: Gao et al. (2023) report that ALCE uses automatic metrics for fluency, correctness, and citation quality and that these metrics correlate strongly with human judgments.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations

label: ALCE ELI5 evaluation found incomplete citation support
summary: Gao et al. (2023) report that even the best models in their ELI5 evaluation lacked complete citation support 50% of the time.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations

label: ContextCite contextual attribution method
summary: Cohen-Wang et al. (2024) introduce ContextCite as a scalable method for attributing generated statements to supplied context, designed to operate on top of existing language models.

sources.title: ContextCite: Attributing Model Generation to Context

label: Three-level evaluation of citation support
summary: Zhang et al. (2024) propose evaluating citation faithfulness metrics against three support levels: full, partial, and no support.

sources.title: Towards Fine-Grained Citation Evaluation in Generated Text: A Comparative Analysis of Faithfulness Metrics

label: No consistently best fine-grained citation faithfulness metric
summary: Zhang et al. (2024) report that no single citation-faithfulness metric consistently performs best across their fine-grained evaluations.

sources.title: Towards Fine-Grained Citation Evaluation in Generated Text: A Comparative Analysis of Faithfulness Metrics

label: Context-prior augmented citation evaluation dimensions
summary: Shen et al. (2025) introduce a citation-generation task considering external context and internal model knowledge, evaluated with five metrics addressing helpfulness, citation faithfulness, and trustworthiness.

sources.title: Transparentize the Internal and External Knowledge Utilization in LLMs with Trustworthy Citation

label: MIRAGE saliency-based answer attribution
summary: Qi et al. (2024) describe MIRAGE as identifying context-sensitive answer tokens and attributing them to retrieved documents using saliency methods.

sources.title: Model Internals-based Answer Attribution for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation

label: Fluent counterfactuals for attribution-faithfulness evaluation
summary: Kamahi et al. (2024) argue that removing or corrupting input tokens creates out-of-distribution inputs for autoregressive language models and propose fluent in-distribution counterfactuals for evaluating attribution methods.

sources.title: Counterfactuals As a Means for Evaluating Faithfulness of Attribution Methods in Autoregressive Language Models

label: CLAIM-BENCH observed scientific claim-evidence reasoning limitations
summary: Javaji et al. (2025) report substantial limitations in processing scientific claim-evidence relationships when evaluating six LLMs on more than 300 claim-evidence pairs across multiple research domains.

sources.title: Can AI Validate Science? Benchmarking LLMs on Claim →Evidence Reasoning in AI Papers

label: Multi-pass prompting tradeoff in CLAIM-BENCH
summary: Javaji et al. (2025) report that three-pass and one-by-one prompting improve LLM claim-to-evidence linking in their evaluations, with increased computational cost.

sources.title: Can AI Validate Science? Benchmarking LLMs on Claim →Evidence Reasoning in AI Papers

label: FaithfulRAG models context-prior conflicts at fact level
summary: Zhang et al. (2025) propose FaithfulRAG, which identifies fact-level conflicts between retrieved context and model knowledge and uses a self-thinking process before generating responses.

sources.title: FaithfulRAG: Fact-Level Conflict Modeling for Context-Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation

label: Reported Context-DPO context-faithfulness improvements
summary: Bi et al. (2025) report Context-DPO context-faithfulness improvements of 35% to 280% on popular open-source models in their experiments.

sources.title: Context-DPO: Aligning Language Models for Context-Faithfulness
